Beejay_88 writes...

"Error: An error has occurred. You may be in the penalty box or Whirlpool may be experiencing issues. Please load Whirlpool in your browser for more details."

That happens when you get HTTP 403 back.

This actually exposes a bug in Whirldroid

Whirldroid is coded to expect HTTP 401 as the code for wrong API key, which Whirlpool API originally said, but at least since 2016, as I updated the wiki then, Whirlpool sends back 403 for this as well

Whirldroid needs to change the error message accordingly

posted 2021-Apr-5, 10:18 pm AEST
O.P.

I've had a quick look at this – some technocrap for those who care: requests made by the app for Whirlpool pages (rather than API endpoints) were using the JSoup library default user agent, which was trying to make the request look like it came from a legit but very old browser. Whirlpool has now started blocking requests from that user agent. I'm now specifying a custom user agent string ("Whirldroid") which seems to be enough to get past the block for now. There's always the chance that requests could start getting blocked again but fingers crossed.

I've published a new version which should fix this up.

womble66 writes...

Was explained somewhere in this thread but simplistically I think it because the thread belongs to a non-public forum.

In theory any non public forum should need to be in a browser, but Home is public.

Whirldroid has a bug/limitation whenever WP adds a new public forum, then it needs to be updated as such

There is a way this can be designed which stops needing manual updates for new forums (unless Simon really does utterly major changes to how forums work...) – I explained it in /thread/97q1vrm9?p=12#r238 but I know it needs more work from Greg rather than the hacky fix when we add forums, so it hasn't been fixed yet

The public forums are hardcoded in https://bitbucket.org/gregdev/whirldroid-2/src/7d10dc9f6f24d2b523038a61ed43cfb9214da800/app/src/main/java/com/gregdev/whirldroid/whirlpool/WhirlpoolApi.java

private static int[] PUBLIC_FORUMS = {92, 100, 142, 82, 9, 107, 135, 80, 136, 125, 116, 63,
            127, 139, 7, 129, 130, 131, 10, 38, 39, 91, 87, 112, 132, 8, 83, 138, 143, 133, 58, 106,
            126, 71, 118, 137, 114, 123, 128, 141, 140, 144, 18, 14, 15, 68, 72, 94, 90, 102, 105,
            109, 108, 147, 31, 67, 5, 148, 149, 150, 151, 152, 153, 154};

As Home Tech aka Forum ID 156 isn't here, it is regarded as a private forum

O.P.

Hi all, it's been a while since I stuck my head in here! Apologies, it wasn't my intention for the app to be removed from the Play Store. Apparently I had been a bit lax in Google's eyes and had to update some data sharing policy stuff, send them my drivers license to prove I'm a human, hand over my firstborn child, etc. That's now done and the app is back up: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gregdev.whirldroid

Obviously it's been a while since the app has been updated, and I don't use it myself any more, but it seems that others still find it useful so please do feel free to email me (you can do this via the app) if there are issues that prevent it from working and I will try to help. Even better if anybody with more free time and motivation wants to fork the app, or just grab bits of code or whatever, to maintain it or build upon and improve it, please go ahead.

IMO, this sort of stuff is easier on a PC if you go to https://play.google.com/apps for pointing me in the right direction!

I was able to successfully trigger an install on my Pixel by using the Google Play web interface:

Step 1: Go to https://play.google.com/apps and search for the app (whirldroid).
Step 2: Target an existing active device first (like an Android emulator/BlueStacks).
Step 3: Refresh the browser tab.

After doing this, my Pixel appeared immediately as an installation option.

From Whirldroid code it seems it uses following logic – https://bitbucket.org/gregdev/whirldroid-2/src/7d10dc9f6f24d2b523038a61ed43cfb9214da800/app/src/main/java/com/gregdev/whirldroid/whirlpool/WhirlpoolApi.java?at=master#lines-617 essentially

$("#top_pagination li").length

Which still works

But there is also https://bitbucket.org/gregdev/whirldroid-2/src/7d10dc9f6f24d2b523038a61ed43cfb9214da800/app/src/main/java/com/gregdev/whirldroid/whirlpool/WhirlpoolApi.java?at=master#lines-319 which doesn't seem to follow the current layout, it's looking for a script element when it should be checking for data-pages in the span element to get page count

Thanks all.

Version 1.0.1 is available now for side-loading at https://github.com/dalbo/whirl/releases/tag/v1.0.1

I think this has more-or-less feature parity with Whirldroid. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Headline features

Whirl 1.0

  • New icon
  • Text size setting for the whole app; posts back to Whirldroid's size
  • Watched refreshes whenever you open the app
  • TalkBack: long-press menus in TalkBack's actions, headings, page changes announced
  • Large text, landscape and tablets: readable posts, nothing cut off
  • "Use wallpaper colours" setting; clearer quote colours
  • "Dark at night" start and end times
  • Multi-part threads: one row with previous/next and a list of parts

On the icon – this one is better than the original placeholder, but is still not anything special. If anyone would like to donate a better icon I'm happy to accept and give credit.

I've submitted it for review with Google Play, and then apparently I need ~12 or more testers for 2 weeks before it can be published in the Play Store. I'll put the word out for official testers when it's ready. Settings should come across from the side-loaded versions.

@Thor – please let me know if there's anything I need to be aware of from the moderator's/website's side of things. I understand that posting from within the app, and attempting to access private forums etc is off-limits. And I have no intent to include ads or other monetisation.

Whirl 1.1.2 is out. Thanks for all the feedback, I think I've covered most of it. Please let me know if I've missed anything

  • Mark as read: there's now a "Mark as read" button at the end of the last page of a watched thread, so you don't need auto mark-read or the menu. (BadFish). And thanks kudabird for picking up that this was showing up more than needed
  • Posts by OP: added to the post filter alongside me, mods and reps. (BadFish)
    • Unfortunately you need to be logged in to see this view, so it will open in your browser. Maybe a future improvement would be to fetch the Archive view (full thread) and filter in the app.
  • Transitions: Settings > Screen animations turns them off. (BadFish)
  • Favourites: these were already there. Long-press a forum in Forums to add it, and favourites show at the top. (BadFish). I assume this is what you're asking about. Let me know if it's some other missing feature.
  • Watched refresh: it now refreshes once when you open the app or come back to it, not every time you return from a thread. (kudabird)
  • Replying in your browser: Settings > "Open Whirlpool pages in the browser app" sends replies, private forums and "Open in browser" to your browser instead of a tab inside Whirl. (Chris)
  • Looks: Settings now has Layout and Colours.
    • Layout: Classic, or Cards. Cards is Jkill's design from his fork, with rounded cards and boxed quotes. Thanks Jkill!
    • Colours: from your wallpaper, Whirl blue, Whirlpool (taken from the site), Whirldroid, or Jkill's Silver & ember. (crunchynuts)
    • Each layout and colour set is a small file in the app, so new ones are easy to add if anyone wants to design one.
  • Re the 16 Unread (kudabird): this was being cached too long, and not being updated in some circumstances. Should be addressed in 1.1.2.

Not yet:

  • Marking a thread read up to a particular post (BRK): as far as I (and Claude) can tell, the API can only mark a whole thread read. Doing it per post would mean Whirl logging in to the site, which isn't something on the radar
  • iOS (FERRARIF1): sorry, not planned. Whirl is Android only, and an iOS version would be a separate app.
